highlights.title: What We Still Don’t Know About OpenAI’s Hugging Face Hack
highlights.summary: The AI giant acknowledges that it could have done far more to prevent its AI agents from going rogue. But it still fails to explain why it didn't see this fiasco coming.
body: OpenAI announced Wednesday that it completed an investigation into what happened when its AI agents hacked into Hugging Face last month and published its most comprehensive report on the incident to date. For the most part, though, the 37-page document raises more questions than it answers, including about what preceded the incident and how OpenAI can stop another one like it from happening again.

What remains especially perplexing is why one of the world’s preeminent AI development labs seemingly underestimated its own models’ capabilities. OpenAI has spent years warning the world about the rapid advancement of AI systems. And yet it failed to implement long-established network security and isolation measures that may have prevented the hacking spree.
“With the benefit of hindsight, some early signals identified in this report could have triggered an earlier response,” OpenAI says in the postmortem.
points: The AI giant acknowledges that it could have done far more to prevent its AI agents from going rogue.
But it still fails to explain why it didn't see this fiasco coming.

“The lawyers at A24 wanted me to sign away my rights to my name, image, and brand, essentially, as well as any potential legal rights that would come out of the movie,” he stated. “I couldn’t sign that, so they didn’t show me the film. I went all the way over there. … But who’s going to sign something like that?

highlights.title: Beyoncé Announces $1 Million Donation for Earthquake Relief Efforts in Colombia
highlights.summary: Beyoncé has announced that she will make a personal donation of $1 million to support relief efforts in Colombia following the country’s recent earthquake. According to a release from Parkwood Entertainment on Tuesday, the donation will provide food and housing supplies to areas most affected by…
body: Beyoncé joins a growing list of musicians who are raising and donating money for earthquake relief in recent weeks. Shakira, a Colombian native, met with Chocó’s governor and mayor to hear about the impact of the earthquake and committed $1.25 million to help rebuild affected schools. That sum included $500,000 from the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, a $500,000 match from the Fund from Live Nation, and $250,000 from CAF.

“These past few days, I’ve watched my country suffer, but I’ve also watched people come together with the resilience and solidarity that has always defined us,” said Shakira in a statement. “Schools are more than buildings. They give children the stability and routine they need most after a disaster. That’s why we’re making an initial $1.25 million commitment to help rebuild schools and get children back into their classrooms. Chocó is not alone. Colombia is not alone. And we will keep going.”

Additionally, Karol G donated $1.2 million to earthquake victims through her foundation, while the Colombian band Morat announced that they will donate a portion of ticket sales from their Bogotá residency.

highlights.title: I tried 11 coffees from Counter Culture, the accessible small-batch roaster converting coffee slobs to snobs
highlights.summary: I’ll never go back to Starbucks after trying this specialty brand. Level up your morning coffee with well-made beans and the right roast for you. Four ways to brew better drip coffee. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I’m an empathetic girl, except when it comes to anyone who despises the taste of coffee.

Having perfected my at-home cup, I can’t fathom anyone disliking the warming flavors that incentivize me to leave my bed every morning. In fact, I’m convinced I could convert tea loyalists and energy drink lovers into coffee connoisseurs if they set aside their Folgers and tried quality beans.

My journey to finding my favorite coffee started with the Starbucks Veranda blend I drank growing up. Then, one day, while browsing my local Whole Foods, I discovered Counter Culture Coffee, an independent specialty coffee brand. I was immediately hooked on its smooth, fresh blends that tasted like the iced coffees I would usually order from my favorite pricey cafes.

Quality aside, I appreciated that Counter Culture was a convenient, reliable option. Often on sale for $12-$16, I found it an accessible way to join the ranks of coffee snobs. While many coffee experts recommend purchasing from a local roaster, I often opt for the convenience of grabbing beans at the grocery store or online. They also offer two subscription options, delivering two bags to your doorstep for under $40 a month.

highlights.title: The inside story on why OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
highlights.summary: The models responsible for last month’s agent hack of Hugging Face had been inadvertently trained to cheat and to communicate with each other, according to an OpenAI technical report released today.
body: Since the hack, OpenAI employees—as well as researchers at the AI evaluation nonprofit METR, which released its own report on the hack today—have worked to understand what went wrong and how similar missteps might be prevented in the future. OpenAI has already put some preventative measures in place based on what they discovered. But making sure AI models do what we want them to do, or “alignment,” remains a gnarly problem, and some of the root causes of the hack will take much longer than a month to resolve.

“It’s not something you can solve overnight,” says Kai Chen, who runs OpenAI’s alignment research team. “There are challenges we’ve been tracking for a very long time, and we’re now seeing them with much greater precision.”

The Hugging Face hack was a product of months of misbehavior from OpenAI agents, first as they were being trained and then as their abilities were being evaluated. This May, agents in training figured out how to use OpenAI’s infrastructure to communicate with one another and get support with difficult training tasks, including some that were impossible to solve without hacking or otherwise misbehaving. That “message board” was shut down.

highlights.title: Portal-Like Shooter Splitgate Died Once, And It’s Dying Again … Kind Of
highlights.summary: Some games just aren't long for this world, and that’s exactly the case with the Portal-like and Halo-like shooter Splitgate: Arena Reloaded, which is getting put on a form of life support starting in early September. Developer 1047 Games took to X on August 26 to announce the news.
body: "The reality is that neither game is generating enough revenue to support the ongoing cost of dedicated servers," 1047 Games said. "We have continued covering the costs because we wanted to give both games every opportunity to grow, but we have reached the point where that is no longer sustainable. We have loved working on these games, playing them, and building them with this community, and we wish we could continue supporting them."

Despite development ending for both games, 1047 Games said that neither one will simply get shut down. Instead, both Empulse and Splitgate: Arena Reloaded have been "reworked to support peer-to-peer play." So, starting September 3, the dedicated servers will go offline, and both games will be playable for the foreseeable future through a P2P server-hosting browser. This means that you'll only be able to find matches when other people are online and hosting games instead of relying on servers to find games for you.

This is exactly what happened with the first Splitgate in August 2025. Released in 2019, the dedicated servers went offline on August 29, 2025, and entered a similar peer-to-peer multiplayer environment.

highlights.title: RIP Tim Curry: Ars remembers his top 10 iconic performances
highlights.summary: It's said celebrity deaths come in threes. We lost Sam Neill last month, and the legendary Dolly Parton yesterday. Now we find out that the universe has also seen fit to deprive us of the glorious presence of Tim Curry, who died at home yesterday in Los Angeles at the age of 80.
body: Throughout his life, he refused to be boxed in or confined to others’ expectations. Across five decades, he moved fluidly between comedy, horror, drama, and music, delighting himself and his legion of fans with his countless dynamic personas. … He is, depending on who you ask, the definitive Dr. Frank-N-Furter, the definitive Pennywise, the man who made a butler’s death-scene monologue in Clue an all-time comedic bit, or simply ‘that unforgettable voice’ from a beloved cartoon of someone’s childhood.

Few actors can claim to have left as many distinct fingerprints on pop culture and though he suffered a debilitating stroke in 2012, he continued adding to his achievements as an artist and, most recently, a writer. Though widely known for his inimitable, flamboyant characters and colorful stage performances, his greatest legacies to those who knew him were his curious, expansive mind and generous, gentle heart, both of which remained open and filled with anticipation until his final breath.

highlights.title: The Humanoids at China’s Robot Games Were Faster Than Usain Bolt—but I’m More Impressed by Their Tweezer Mastery
highlights.summary: Beijing’s endlessly delightful Robot Games featured tons of impressive stunts. But the most mind-blowing tricks challenged the humanoid’s brain, not its brawn.
body: If you’re anything like me, the World Humanoid Robot Games are a highlight of your sporting calendar.

The event, held in China, showcases the latest humanoid hardware, lots of algorithmic innovations, and a good dose of robot slapstick. This year’s iteration, which wrapped up in Beijing on August 26, did not disappoint. Besides record-breaking feats—the fastest humanoid on the planet!—and the occasional calamity—weightlifting gone wrong!—the games also included some new challenges that hint at the event’s real purpose: pushing humanoid companies to develop systems that inch closer and closer to practical deployment.
First, though, let’s marvel at some of the more dramatic happenings, which have been all over the internet since things kicked off on August 22.

The opening ceremony showcased the sheer size of the event—the organizers say that more than 600 teams showed up with over 2,000 robots. There are more than 100 humanoid robot manufacturers in China alone, and participants also traveled in from 15 other countries.

highlights.title: Ridley Scott Is Developing an Alien: Covenant Sequel With Michael Fassbender
highlights.summary: Ridley Scott has confirmed he isn't done with the Alien franchise, as he's developing a sequel to Alien: Covenant. When speaking with the LA Times, Scott confirmed he is still developing a sequel to Alien: Covenant, one that would follow Michael Fassbender's character, David.
body: The end of Covenant teased that his story was far from over, but that follow-up film has been in development hell for nearly a decade. Covenant itself missed the mark financially, and then Fox was acquired by Disney, which likely caused all kinds of issues with the film's development. Still, the Alien IP is very active with FX's Alien: Earth series and 2024's Alien: Romulus, which was a big hit. There's also the highly-anticipated Alien: Isolation 2 on the horizon for gamers.

Ridley Scott had previously stated that he wanted to make a whole series of Alien prequels that lead into the original film, and his follow-up to Covenant would be one of many entries to build up to that. As of right now, it's unclear when Ridley Scott plans to break out the chestbursters again. He just released The Dog Stars, starring Jacob Elordi ( which IGN gave a 5 ), and has a Treasure Planet adaptation with Hugh Jackman set to begin filming in November, a Bee Gees project at Paramount, and a variety of original films in different stages of development.

highlights.title: Nvidia is about to be a hundred-billion-dollar-a-quarter company
highlights.summary: Nvidia's predicting it will pull in $108 billion in revenue within just a few months. It wouldn't be the first company to rake in over $100 billion in quarterly revenue - Amazon, Apple, and Alphabet have repeatedly reached the milestone.
body: The chip company made over $96 billion in the past quarter, most of it from its data center business.

Nvidia said in its latest earnings report that it brought in a record $96.2 billion in overall revenue in the past quarter, a jump of over $10 billion from the previous quarter. Its data center revenue alone more than doubled year-over-year to a record $89 billion, and the company’s profits more than doubled to $59.7 billion.

Nvidia’s “edge computing” category, which includes its consumer gaming business, accounted for just $7.2 billion of its revenue last quarter. That’s a 27 percent increase year-over-year, but Nvidia acknowledged that it experienced “slower consumer PC sales that were tempered by elevated memory and systems prices.” Component shortages continue to drive up prices for Nvidia’s consumer GPUs, and it also warned of price hikes for its AI chips ahead of Wednesday’s earnings report.

highlights.title: Candidates Are Signing a Pact Promising Action on Data Centers and AI Safety
highlights.summary: More than 15 politicians from across the country have signed on to the AI Pact, vowing to regulate data centers and AI. “We’ve got to get this right,” says Senate candidate Dan Osborn of Nebraska.
body: Dan Osborn was finishing up his fourth town hall last Sunday, he says, when a “hardcore MAGA” guy approached him. Osborn, who is running for the US Senate in Nebraska as an independent against Republican incumbent Pete Ricketts, said that he and the man didn’t have much common ground—at first.
“Then I said, ‘Hey, what’s your take on AI and data centers?’” Osborn says. “Boy, right away, we were in lockstep, 100 percent agreement.”

Osborn is one of more than 15 politicians running for office in states across the country who have signed on to the AI Pact, a set of five promises around regulating both data centers and AI itself. As concerns about data centers have exploded in the midterm cycle, politicians are scrambling to respond to voters’ worries about their environmental impacts, the secrecy surrounding their construction, and the corporate power behind them. The new pledge is intended, according to its website, to provide “a needed baseline to ensure a humanity-first future.”

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: My mum has died – and there is one kind of response I can’t stand | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: The platitudes, euphemisms and cliches are excruciating. But the people who say nothing at all are the worst. Luckily, I already knew having a comic thought at a tragic moment is a natural stress response, or I might have worried.
body: In Curb Your Enthusiasm, when Marty Funkhouser’s mother’s wheelchair was run over by a car, he proclaimed himself an orphan. David informed him he was too old to be an orphan. Funkhouser insisted that if your parents are dead, you’re an orphan.

Images of Annie-like red curls aside, the people who brought you into the world both having left it is pretty profound. I’m lucky to have a lot of support, but it’s a hard knock in life. A singularly specific brand of aloneness; the natural order that feels anything but. It’s so weird. There’s no one to tell me off any more, either. I wonder what I may get up to. What if I fall in with a bad crowd?

My mum “had a good innings though”, as I have been reminded roughly thrice daily. It’s been 14 years since my dad died, and there’s so much I’d forgotten about the grief game – namely the platitudes, the strange language, and how terrible so many of us are at dealing with it. The best reaction so far was a bloke who replied to my breaking of the news for sadmin purposes with: “OK, that’s fine.” At least he gave me a good story.

body: Reuters’ report highlights the challenges organizations face when analyzing the best uses for AI and determining when the technology is a better fit for certain tasks than employees.

Meta confirmed to Reuters that the plan, reportedly codenamed Project OT (short for organization transformation), explored scenarios in which Meta reduced some team headcounts by 60 percent and that the plan called for two rounds of layoffs. Meta wouldn’t confirm which teams Project OT affected.

As part of our company restructuring earlier this year, we asked some teams to conduct a scenario planning exercise looking at the potential impact of redeployments, open role closures and cuts. This ultimately resulted in moving thousands of employees to do priority work on several newly-established teams, as has been publicly reported. Ultimately, we didn’t move forward with every scenario from the exercise – and it was never assumed we would.

It was a winning return ⁠to the Bernabéu for Mourinho, more than 13 years after his previous home match in charge of the club, as Madrid recovered from a disjointed first half ⁠with a ruthless display after the break.
Madrid were jeered before half-time after a sluggish opening in which they ​looked short of rhythm, careless in possession and ‌vulnerable on the counterattack.

“There’s always a sense of justice in the ​boos and the applause, and the odd boo now ‌and then doesn’t do anyone any ‌harm – it helps you grow,” Mourinho said at full time. “We all know the Santiago Bernabéu and just how demanding the fans ‌are here, and I’m very pleased with how my players responded under pressure and put in a great second half, in which we could even have scored more goals.”

Our collagen production may naturally start to decrease in our mid-to-late 20s, explains Morgan Rabach, MD, board-certified dermatologist at Rabach Aesthetics. When you add in air pollution, sun exposure, inflammation, stress, poor sleep, and other external factors, that’s when collagen really weakens and you’ll start to notice those first signs of aging: fine lines, sagging skin, etc. If you’re not facing severe skin laxity that requires the more intense skin-firming treatments, topical products will be your first line of defense.

highlights.title: Democrats Just Might Win the Senate
highlights.summary: Strategists in both parties have long thought that everything would need to go right for Democrats to take over Congress this fall. Their map, though, is becoming more forgiving.
body: With primary elections in the key 2026 battleground states largely complete, Democrats have emerged with several open paths to take the majority in the US Senate.

The basic contours of the national map remain uphill for Democrats. They currently hold 47 seats in the Senate, meaning they need to flip four Republican seats and hold their current ones, including in Michigan and Georgia, which President Donald Trump won in 2024.

But presiding over an unpopular Iran war that has dragged on for six months and resulted in high gas and grocery prices, Trump’s approval rating is now consistently below 40 percent, a historically perilous level. A Reuters/Ipsos poll has shown his approval nearing 30 percent.

The last time a Republican president was presiding over an unpopular war and spiking gas prices with less than 40 percent approval—George W. Bush in 2006—Democrats picked up six seats and took control of the Senate.

highlights.title: AI Slop Is Ruining Cute Animals on the Internet
highlights.summary: Pet owners, rescue agencies, and wildlife groups are calling for new safeguards as AI makes it harder to tell whether animals, from polar bears to house cats, are real or fake.
body: AI-generated videos and pictures are destroying one of the largest and most enduring sources of joy and compassion on the internet: animals. Whether the imagery features sailors rescuing a polar bear, baby cows separated from their mothers, or a lost pet that was miraculously found, many people have reached the point where they can’t take the creatures on their feeds at face value anymore. The explosion of deepfakes and AI slop over the past few years has led to widespread frustration among viewers, creators, and organizations that support animals, forcing everyone to hunt in the pixels for glitches or other telltale signs of AI.

Mibbby Butler was overjoyed one day in April when she received a text message that her lost cat, Brooklyn, had supposedly been found. Her roommate’s boyfriend had allegedly taken the cat and dumped him 30 minutes away in the Los Angeles suburbs the day prior. Butler quickly posted a missing poster on social media, and she was driving around with her roommate searching for Brooklyn when a stranger sent her a photo. In it, he is sitting on a kitchen counter while being embraced by a girl.

body: Cake goop – a mix of flour, oil and butter – is a gift of guaranteed cake release that I found on the internet, and it means no more stuck bundts. Bless the baker who invented it! Goop has it all – release, plus enough sticking power to hold the batter as it rises and cools, without slumping. Additionally, mixing the flour with oil means you don’t get that fine, white, dusty crust on the outside of the cooked cake. Goop is 100% reliable with a 100% untarnished release record in my kitchen.

If you do have a small stuck piece of cake, shimmy it out of the tin with an offset spatula and patch it back on to the cake while warm. Pretty easy! If a whole ring of cake has stuck, cut it into workable sections, prise each out and place back on the cake. Drench the bundt with icing sugar after its soak to hide the Franken-bundt’s monster appearance.

The recipe calls for the eggs to be warmed before cracking. Warmer-than-room- temperature eggs emulsify into the creamed base better, and an emulsified mix means no “curdled” appearance. To do this, submerge the uncracked eggs in hot tap water for five minutes.
